This is not fully correct. While it might work you would very likely incur in problems.

https://web.archive.org/web/20060314132347/http://cma.zdnet.com/book/upgraderepair/ch13/ch13.htm

Scroll down to "Disk Magnetic Properties" for an explanation of the problem.

Also, scroll down to "Floppy Disk Media Types and Specifications" for a table with the magnetic field strength used by the different formats.

So yeah, while it could work, or look like working, it would be risky for your data to be written on the wrong kind of medium. A magnetic field too weak could result in bad sectors or unsafe data (magnetization that degrades with time), a too strong magnetic field could easily destroy data on nearby tracks.

In short... floppy disk drives knew how much current to use to write data using the holes that told it what kind of media it was using (DD or HD)... by cheating you are writing data on the media with a magnetic field strength that is out of specifications for that media.
